item.title: Reliable Conflation of Road Networks: A Group‐Based Optimization Model
item.description: Transactions in GIS, Volume 30, Issue 7, November 2026.
item.dc:description: ABSTRACT Geospatial data conflation involves matching and merging the corresponding objects in two different maps of the same geographic area. Road networks have been a focus of conflation research since 1980s due to their importance in urban and transportation systems and common needs in day‐to‐day GIS analysis. A challenge in conflating two GIS road networks is that roads may be represented differently. A road can be represented as one object in one dataset but as multiple objects in another dataset causing partial matches. In optimization‐based conflation, partial matches between objects are generally handled by using half distances to measure the likelihood of membership (m:1) relation between features. However, partial match relations are error‐prone and more difficult to handle. In this article, we propose a new approach for handling partial matches by restoring them into one‐to‐one matches. Methodologically, we consider all possible ways of grouping road segments into longer lines or paths, and then optimally match these paths instead of original road segments. Experiments show that the proposed group‐based matching model outperforms conventional element‐based models by nearly 40% in terms of both recall and precision in fragmented road datasets.
item.content:encoded:
ABSTRACT

Geospatial data conflation involves matching and merging the corresponding objects in two different maps of the same geographic area. Road networks have been a focus of conflation research since 1980s due to their importance in urban and transportation systems and common needs in day-to-day GIS analysis. A challenge in conflating two GIS road networks is that roads may be represented differently. A road can be represented as one object in one dataset but as multiple objects in another dataset causing partial matches. In optimization-based conflation, partial matches between objects are generally handled by using half distances to measure the likelihood of membership (m:1) relation between features. However, partial match relations are error-prone and more difficult to handle. In this article, we propose a new approach for handling partial matches by restoring them into one-to-one matches. Methodologically, we consider all possible ways of grouping road segments into longer lines or paths, and then optimally match these paths instead of original road segments. Experiments show that the proposed group-based matching model outperforms conventional element-based models by nearly 40% in terms of both recall and precision in fragmented road datasets.
